source.title: Deep Neural Network to Describe the Measurement of the Higgs Production in the Full Leptonic Channel via Vector Boson Fusion
source.citation: Félix Napoleón Díaz Desposorio et al., 2023
source.authors: Félix Napoleón Díaz Desposorio; L. J. Sánchez Rosas; Jhonny Jonnatan Rojas Hancco

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains a DNN for signal/background discrimination, but does not test memorization of random labels or the listed generalization claims. Its optimizer and dropout discussion does not compare their effects on held-out performance.
record.gate_note: The paper reports classifier performance and train/validation plots, but gives no result comparing dropout, optimizer, model size, or other listed conditions on the train-test gap. It does not report random-label fitting or natural-label generalization after memorization.
record.test_reason: The study uses dropout to mitigate overfitting and reports its physics classifier's performance. It provides no comparative results testing dropout, optimizer, width, batch size, or any other claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their DNN separates VBF signal from the main backgrounds and that fitting the classifier-score distribution yields expected significances of 2.2σ for VBF and 2.8σ for Higgs.
record.recipe_differences: A fully connected DNN trained with Adam for a simulated physics classification task; no random-label memorization or generalization comparison is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says results depend on tuning parameters and reports testing configurations by trial and error, but does not state which choices changed the claimed generalization behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: The DNN has a reported AUC range of 82%–98% across the low and high MJJ regions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A fully connected DNN discriminates simulated VBF signal from background in the studied physics setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the LACCEI international multi-conference for engineering, education and technology
record.problems: The paper says it trained and evaluated on the same dataset for simplicity, then describes an 80/20 training/testing split. Its performance figures are plots without numeric train-test comparisons in the text, and the reported AUC range is not assigned to each region.
record.rows_left_out: No further claim-relevant results are reported. Figures 4–9 show training/validation or training/testing performance, but provide no textual numeric values or comparisons tied to a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; configuration candidates alone provide no result.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets; only Adam is evaluated.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes; candidate batch sizes have no comparative results.
Dropout's effect on held-out error relative to no dropout, including training-set size and dropout-strength conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Test accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: General statements about dropout and Adam are background assertions, not comparative findings. The text inconsistently describes evaluation on the training dataset and an 80/20 training/testing split. These ambiguities do not establish evidence for any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Large versus small batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout versus no dropout effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: DNN models for low and high MJJ regions
rows.size_stated: Fully connected network; tested 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 hidden layers and 4 to 10 K nodes per layer; best configuration not stated.
rows.value: 82 % to 98 % for the low and high MJJ regions
rows.note: The paper reports a range across two regions without assigning a separate value to either. It reports classifier separability, not a train-test gap or comparison relevant to the listed versions.
rows.check: The reported AUC range of 82%–98% is supported, but measures signal/background discrimination rather than any listed effect. Values are not assigned separately to the two regions, and the evaluation split is described inconsistently.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
